images.title: One more column, one row less
images.purpose: Show with squares why 7 × 15 is the known product plus 7 and why 6 × 14 is the known product minus 14: the new column has one square in each of the 7 rows, and the removed row has 14 squares.
images.composition: Two arrays side by side. Left: the 7 by 14 array of teal squares with one extra green column of 7 squares added at its right edge. Right: the 7 by 14 array whose last row of 14 squares is drawn white with a dashed edge, as the row that is taken away.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, with one thin construction grey #6B7280 vertical line at x 728 from y 130 to y 700 between two panels. Every square is 30 px by 30 px with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (2 px), and squares are 4 px apart (a pitch of 34 px). Panel headings, dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px), centred at y 190: One more column at x 363 over the left panel and One row less at x 1066 over the right panel. LEFT PANEL: an array of exactly 7 rows by 15 columns of squares (105 squares), spanning x 110 to 616 and y 250 to 484. The first 14 columns (x 110 to 586, 98 squares) are filled teal #0072B2. The 15th column (x 586 to 616, exactly 7 squares, one in each row) is filled green #009E73. RIGHT PANEL: an array of exactly 7 rows by 14 columns of squares (98 squares), spanning x 830 to 1302 and y 250 to 484. The first 6 rows (y 250 to 450, 84 squares) are filled teal #0072B2. The 7th row (y 454 to 484, exactly 14 squares) is white with a dashed grey #6B7280 outline (3 px dashes), as a row that is taken away. Under the left array, centred at x 363: the line 7 × 15 = 98 + 7 at y 560 (bold, 42 px, dark) and the words Add 7 at y 630 (36 px, dark). Under the right array, centred at x 1066: the line 6 × 14 = 98 − 14 at y 560 (bold, 42 px, dark) and the words Take away 14 at y 630 (36 px, dark). In all there are 203 squares: 98 teal and 7 green on the left, 84 teal and 14 dashed white on the right. No other numbers, no arrows, no row or column counts. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: One more column adds as many squares as there are rows, and one row less takes away as many squares as there are in a row, so the new product is the known product plus 7 or minus 14.
images.description: Two arrays of squares: 7 rows of 14 with one extra green column of 7 squares, and the same array with its last row of 14 squares drawn dashed as the row taken away.
images.context: Concept image for Grow from a Known Product. It follows the idea of the arrays in your maths book (a known array with one extra column or one extra row coloured) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 7 × 14 = 98, 7 × 15 and 6 × 14.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child which number is added: the new column has 7 squares, not 14. The slip to watch: adding the number that was already multiplied.

image_decisions.why: The array with one extra column and the array with one row taken away show at a glance why the number added is 7 and the number taken away is 14, which is the point of growing from a known product.
